questions.question:
39762. Which phospholipid participates in neural signaling and neurotransmission?
(কোন ফসফোলিপিড স্নায়বিক সংকেত ও নিউরোট্রান্সমিশনে অংশগ্রহণ করে?)
questions.explain:
→Phosphatidyl-serine is important in brain cell membranes and helps in neurotransmission.
(ফসফাটিডাইল-সেরিন মস্তিষ্কের কোষঝিল্লিতে থাকে এবং নিউরোট্রান্সমিশনে সাহায্য করে।)

→Cephalin (phosphatidyl-ethanolamine) plays a vital role in blood clotting.
(সেফালিন রক্ত জমাট বাঁধার প্রক্রিয়ায় গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ভূমিকা পালন করে।)

→Lecithin (phosphatidyl-choline) is the main component of lung surfactant that reduces surface tension in alveoli, preventing collapse.
(লেসিথিন ফুসফুসে সারফ্যাকট্যান্ট তৈরি করে, যা অ্যালভিওলাই-এর সারফেস টেনশন কমায় এবং ধসে পড়া থেকে রক্ষা করে।)

→Phosphatidyl-inositol is a key molecule in signal transduction pathways and regulates cell membrane activities.
(ফসফাটিডাইল-ইনোসিটল সংকেত পরিবহনের জন্য অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ এবং কোষঝিল্লির কার্যকলাপ নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে।)

questions.question:
39761. Which of the following types of lipids make up 98–99% of food and body fats?
(নিচের কোন ধরনের লিপিড খাদ্য ও শরীরের চর্বির ৯৮–৯৯% গঠন করে)?
questions.explain:
Simple lipids, also known as neutral fats, are made up of triglycerides (glycerol + three fatty acids). These neutral fats constitute about 98–99% of the fats found in food and the human body.
(সিম্পল লিপিড বা নিউট্রাল ফ্যাট ট্রাইগ্লিসারাইড দিয়ে গঠিত, যেখানে গ্লিসারল এর সাথে তিনটি ফ্যাটি এসিড যুক্ত থাকে। খাদ্য ও শরীরের চর্বির প্রায় ৯৮–৯৯% এই নিউট্রাল ফ্যাট দিয়ে গঠিত।)

questions.question: 39760. Triglycerides with a high proportion of unsaturated fatty acids are called:(যে ট্রাইগ্লিসারাইডে আনস্যাচুরেটেড ফ্যাটি এসিড বেশি থাকে তাকে বলা হয় : )
questions.explain:
When triglycerides contain mostly unsaturated fatty acids, they are liquid at room temperature and are called oils.
Common sources include olive oil, canola oil, peanut oil, etc.
(ট্রাইগ্লিসারাইডে আনস্যাচুরেটেড ফ্যাটি এসিড বেশি থাকলে এগুলো সাধারণত কক্ষ তাপমাত্রায় তরল অবস্থায় থাকে এবং এদের অয়েল বলা হয়।
এর প্রধান উৎস হলো অলিভ অয়েল, ক্যানোলা অয়েল, চিনাবাদাম তেল ইত্যাদি।)

questions.question: 39759. In the land of the Houyhnhnms, what is the one concept that the rational horses have no word for and cannot comprehend?
questions.explain:
The society of the Houyhnhnms is governed entirely by reason and truth. Their language is a perfect reflection of this, as they believe the purpose of speech is simply to communicate reality.

When Gulliver tries to explain the concept of a lie, his Houyhnhnm master cannot understand it. The idea of saying "the thing which was not" is completely alien to their nature. They have no word for it because the concept itself does not exist in their society. This inability to comprehend deception is the ultimate mark of their innocence and rationality, and it serves as Swift's most powerful critique of a human society built on dishonesty and misrepresentation.

questions.question: 39758. The King of Brobdingnag believes that the best qualification for a legislator is:
questions.option4: A deep understanding of philosophy and law
questions.explain:
This is one of the most bitingly satirical lines in the book. The answer is ironic. The King of Brobdingnag does not actually believe these are good qualities.

Instead, after listening to Gulliver's detailed and proud explanation of the English Parliament and its members, the King makes this sarcastic conclusion. Based on Gulliver's own account of how politicians are elected (often through wealth and influence) and how they behave (engaging in corruption, factionalism, and self-interest), the King ironically states that Gulliver has "clearly proved, that ignorance, idleness, and vice, are the proper ingredients for qualifying a legislator."

The King's statement is a harsh criticism of the English political system, suggesting that it is so flawed that it rewards the worst qualities in people rather than the best.

questions.question: 39757. What is the shocking realization Gulliver comes to when he observes the Yahoos?
questions.option1: That they are an enchanted species of monkey.
questions.option2: That they are a degenerate form of human being.
questions.option3: That they are the larval stage of the Houyhnhnms.
questions.option4: That they are colonists from a rival European nation.
questions.explain:
This is the central, horrifying climax of Gulliver's travels and the core of Swift's satire in the final voyage.

Initially, Gulliver is disgusted by the Yahoos and tries to distance himself from them, emphasizing to the Houyhnhnms that he is different. However, as he spends more time observing their brutish, greedy, lustful, and violent behavior, he is forced to confront the undeniable truth: the Yahoos are a raw, uncivilized version of his own species.

The "shocking realization" is that the vices he sees in the Yahoos—their fights over worthless shiny stones (greed), their filthiness, their mindless aggression—are the same vices that drive human society in Europe, only hidden under a thin veneer of clothing and social customs. He sees humanity stripped of its pretensions, and the image is so repulsive that it leads to his eventual misanthropy and breakdown.

questions.question: 39756. What physical feature of the Brobdingnagians does Gulliver find particularly disgusting and magnified due to their immense size?
questions.option2: The blemishes and imperfections on their skin
questions.explain:
Because of his tiny size, Gulliver is able to observe the Brobdingnagians at a "microscopic" level. This close-up perspective reveals every flaw that would be invisible at a normal scale. He is particularly disgusted by the sight of their skin, which he describes in great detail. He sees moles as large as dinner plates, pores he could fall into, and coarse hairs as thick as rope.

This detailed and unflattering description is a key part of Swift's satire. It serves to strip away any idealized notions of beauty and show that even the "fairest" skin is full of imperfections when examined too closely. It highlights the theme of relativity—what appears beautiful from one perspective can be grotesque from another.

questions.question: 39755. Where was Gulliver living in the capital of Liliput? In -
questions.explain: When Gulliver was brought to the capital of Lilliput, the Lilliputians had to find a structure large enough to house him. They chose the largest building in their kingdom, which was an ancient temple that had been abandoned and considered "profane" after a murder was committed there. Gulliver was chained by one leg to this temple, which served as his home during his stay. The great gate was tall enough for him to creep through, and he could lie down comfortably inside.

questions.question: 39754. In Liliput Gulliver is called-
questions.explain: The Lilliputians, being only six inches tall, were astounded by Gulliver's enormous size. They gave him the name "Quinbus Flestrin," which translates to "Man-Mountain" in their language.

questions.question: 39753. Swift's creation of new words and languages for the different lands Gulliver visits, such as "Lilliput" and "Houyhnhnm," is a demonstration of his mastery of what?
questions.explain: Jonathan Swift's creation of unique names and languages for the fantastical lands Gulliver visits is a prime example of linguistic fabrication. He invents these words to build a believable and immersive world for his satire. Words like "Lilliput," "Brobdingnag," "Houyhnhnm," and "Yahoo" are not historically accurate (A), nor do they relate to poetic rhythm (C) or a specific character's speech (D). Instead, they are entirely new coinages designed to give each society its own distinct identity, enhancing the satirical commentary and the overall world-building of the novel.

questions.question: 39752. Gulliver's ambition was-
questions.explain:
While Lemuel Gulliver undertakes several voyages, his primary and enduring ambition was to travel all the world. Initially, Gulliver's travels are partly motivated by financial necessity. After his business as a surgeon in London fails, he goes to sea to earn a living. However, a deeper-seated love for adventure and exploration is consistently portrayed as his main driving force. He is described as a curious and intelligent Englishman who repeatedly leaves his home and family to have adventures in distant lands.

Even after enduring harrowing experiences, including shipwrecks, captivity, and facing immense dangers, his desire to see the world is not diminished. For instance, despite his intention to stay home after one of his voyages, he accepts the captaincy of a merchant ship because he is bored with his life as a surgeon. This recurring theme throughout "Gulliver's Travels" highlights that his ultimate ambition was the journey and the discovery of new places and societies, rather than the accumulation of wealth or power.

questions.question: 39751. The conflict between the two nations began after an Emperor of Lilliput's son injured himself, leading to an edict on how to break eggs. The citizens who defied this edict and fled for protection to the rival empire are known by what name?
questions.explain:
The conflict between the two nations, Lilliput and Blefuscu, began after the Emperor of Lilliput's grandfather, as a boy, injured himself while breaking an egg on its larger end. This incident prompted his father, the reigning emperor, to issue an edict commanding all his subjects to break their eggs on the smaller end. This decree was met with significant resistance from the populace, leading to six rebellions and the loss of one emperor's life and another's crown.

Those who defied the edict and continued the traditional practice of breaking their eggs at the larger end were known as the "Big-Endians". Facing persecution, these Big-Endians fled for protection to the rival empire of Blefuscu. The books of the Big-Endians were also forbidden in Lilliput. The other terms mentioned, "The Tramecksan" and "The Slamecksan," refer to political factions in Lilliput distinguished by the height of their heels and are not related to the egg-breaking controversy. "The Little-Endians" were those who complied with the emperor's edict.

questions.question: 39750. "the most pernicious Race of little odious Vermin that Nature ever suffered to crawl upon the Surface of the Earth" is said by whom?
questions.explain:
- In the second voyage Gulliver was a tiny creature among the giants, so he tried to overcome his physical miniature through patriotism. He boastfull described about his nation and got this reaction.

- This scathing assessment of humanity is delivered by the King of the giant land of Brobdingnag After Lemuel Gulliver proudly describes the society, politics, and history of Europe, and specifically England, the King is horrified. Based on Gulliver's own accounts of conspiracies, rebellions, murders, and massacres, the King concludes that the English must be "the most pernicious Race of little odious Vermin that Nature ever suffered to crawl upon the Surface of the Earth".

- This quote is one of the most famous from Jonathan Swift's "Gulliver's Travels" and serves as a powerful satire of European civilization. The King's reaction highlights Gulliver's own blindness to the deep flaws of his own society.

questions.question: 39749. When Gulliver first wakes up in Lilliput, what is his condition?
questions.option1: He is in a comfortable bed, well-fed and rested.
questions.option2: He is lying on his back, with his arms, legs, and hair tied to the ground.
questions.option3: He is running from the Lilliputians, trying to escape them.
questions.option4: He is being carried to the capital city in a large cage.
questions.explain:
In Gulliver's Travels, Gulliver's ship was caught in a violent storm. The vessel is thrown off course, hits a rock, and breaks apart. Gulliver, a skilled swimmer, manages to escape the wreck and swim until he reaches the shore of Lilliput. 
After swimming to shore from his shipwreck and falling into a deep sleep from exhaustion, Gulliver awakens to find himself completely immobilized. The Lilliputians have used a vast number of slender, but strong, threads to stake his limbs and even his long hair to the ground, effectively capturing him before he was even aware of their presence.

questions.question: 39748. What happens to Gulliver's ship, the Antelope, leading to his arrival in Lilliput?
questions.option2: It is wrecked in a violent storm.
questions.option3: The crew mutinies and abandons him.
questions.option4: It runs aground on a hidden sandbar.
questions.explain: In Voyage 1, we see Gulliver's voyage on the Antelope begins well, but the ship is eventually caught in a violent storm. The vessel is thrown off course, hits a rock, and breaks apart. Gulliver, a skilled swimmer, manages to escape the wreck and swim until he reaches the shore of Lilliput. Exhausted from his ordeal, he falls asleep on the beach, where he is discovered and captured by the tiny inhabitants. That is the begining of this fantasy travelogue.

questions.question: 39747. What weapons do the Lilliputians use against Gulliver when they first encounter him?
questions.option4: Nets and ropes to capture him.
questions.explain: When Gulliver first awakens on the shore of Lilliput and struggles against his bonds, the tiny inhabitants respond with an organized military assault. They fire a volley of thousands of tiny arrows at him, which he describes as pricking him like needles, particularly on his hands and face. This attack, though not causing serious injury, is painful and demonstrates their numbers and determination, convincing Gulliver to lie still.

questions.question: 39746. Gulliver is able to gain passage through Japan by pretending to be-
questions.explain:
In Jonathan Swift's "Gulliver's Travels," Gulliver is able to secure passage through Japan by pretending to be a Dutch trader. At the time the novel was written, Japan had a strict policy of isolation and the Dutch were the only Europeans permitted to enter the country for trade. Gulliver adopts this disguise out of necessity, as it is his only viable route back to Europe from the island of Luggnagg. The King of Luggnagg assists him by providing a letter of recommendation to the Emperor of Japan.

This part of the story also serves as a vehicle for Swift's satire. When asked to perform the ceremony of trampling on a crucifix, a test imposed on the Dutch to prove they were not Christians, Gulliver manages to be excused from the practice. The Emperor of Japan is surprised by this refusal, remarking that Gulliver was the first "Dutchman" to ever object, which makes him question if Gulliver is a "real Hollander." This incident is used by Swift to criticize the perceived willingness of the Dutch to forsake their faith for commercial gain.

questions.question: 39745. The King of Laputa can control the land below by-
questions.option4: Hovering over a town to block the sun and rain
questions.explain:
The King of Laputa, the flying island in Jonathan Swift's "Gulliver's Travels," maintains control over the land of Balnibarbi below through a unique and oppressive method. By positioning the floating island directly over a rebellious town, he can deprive its inhabitants of sunlight and rain, thereby causing famine and disease.

As further punishment, the Laputians can also drop rocks on the towns below. In the most extreme cases of rebellion, the king has the ultimate power to lower the entire island and crush the city beneath it. This technological superiority allows the king and the educated elite, who reside on Laputa, to enforce their rule without the need for a traditional army. The floating island itself serves as a powerful weapon and a constant, visible symbol of the government's dominance over its subjects on the ground.

questions.question: 39744. At what age are struldbrugs declared legally dead?
questions.explain:
The Struldbrugs are a fictional group of people from Jonathan Swift's satirical novel, Gulliver's Travels. Residing on the island of Luggnagg, they are born seemingly normal but are, in fact, immortal. However, their immortality is a curse rather than a blessing, as they are not granted eternal youth and continue to age, suffering from the physical and mental declines of old age. These unfortunate immortals are identifiable by a red dot above their left eyebrow at birth, which changes color over time, turning black by the age of forty. They live ordinary lives until about thirty years old, after which they become increasingly melancholy and dejected.

Upon reaching the age of eighty, Struldbrugs are declared legally dead. At this point, their heirs inherit their estates, with only a small amount reserved for their support. They are forbidden from owning property, holding employment, or even being witnesses in legal matters.
The lives of the Struldbrugs are marked by a host of miseries. They are described as "opinionative, peevish, covetous, morose, vain, [and] talkative." Furthermore, they are incapable of friendship and lose all natural affection. Their memory fades, leaving them with only imperfect recollections of their youth and middle age. This memory loss is so severe that it is considered safer to rely on common tradition than on their accounts of the past.The most pitiable among them are those who descend into dementia, as they are spared some of the negative qualities that plague others.
A significant challenge for the Struldbrugs is the ever-changing nature of language. Over time, the language of Luggnagg evolves to the point that older Struldbrugs can no longer communicate with the current generation, making them "foreigners in their own country."

Swift uses the Struldbrugs to critique the human desire for immortality, demonstrating that an endless life without youth and vitality would be a miserable existence. Gulliver's initial excitement at the prospect of meeting immortals is shattered when he witnesses their wretched state, leading him to see death as a welcome release. The Struldbrugs serve as a powerful satire on the fear of aging and the folly of wishing for a life that never ends.

questions.question: 39743. Who is considered the greatest satirist of English literature?
questions.explain:
Jonathan Swift is widely regarded as the greatest satirist of English literature. Because Swift's work addresses social, political, and moral issues, employing irony and exaggeration. His style has influenced countless writers and remains relevant in discussions of satire today.
Some of his famous works became symbol of true satire, like 
"A Modest Proposal": A satirical essay that critiques British policy towards the Irish.
"Gulliver's Travels": A novel that uses fantastical voyages to satirize human nature and society. 
Actually Swift's unique blend of humor and sharp critique solidifies his status in literary history.

questions.question: 39742. At Voyage 3, A professor at the Academy has a plan to abolish words and have people communicate by-
questions.option2: Pointing at objects they carry in sacks
questions.option3: A universal system of hand gestures
questions.explain:
Jonathan Swift's "Gulliver's Travels, Voyage 3 is a satire on Science and Knowledge which are absurd and impractical. To show its acuteness Swift gave that situation in this novel.  A professor at the Academy of Lagado, featured " proposed a plan to abolish all words entirely. To communicate, individuals would carry with them all the objects necessary to express themselves and simply point to the relevant item.

This unconventional method was suggested as a way to promote health and brevity, arguing that speaking contributes to the corrosion of the lungs and the shortening of one's life. The plan was met with some support from the learned and wise, who would be seen carrying large bundles of objects on their backs to facilitate conversation. However, the scheme was ultimately opposed by women, the vulgar, and the illiterate, who insisted on the freedom to speak with their tongues as their ancestors had.

questions.question: 39741. Which of the following is NOT an application of solar energy? নিচের কোনটি সৌরশক্তির ব্যবহার নয়?
questions.explain:
Solar energy comes from the sun's radiation in the form of heat and light.
It is renewable and is used for:
Generating electricity (solar panels)
Heating (solar heaters)
Cooking (solar cookers)
Drying food, etc.
Nuclear power, on the other hand:
Comes from atomic reactions (nuclear fission or fusion).
It uses uranium or plutonium fuel, not sunlight.
Therefore, solar energy cannot generate nuclear power because they are based on completely different processes.

questions.question: 39740. Which of the following combinations shows complementary color harmony?
questions.explain:
​A complementary color harmony is a combination of two colors that are directly opposite each other on the color wheel. These pairs create the strongest contrast.
​a) Blue, Green, Yellow is a combination of analogous colors, which are next to each other on the color wheel.
​b) Pink, Blue are not a complementary pair.
​c) Red, Orange, Yellow is also a combination of analogous colors.
​d) Light Blue, Sky Blue is a monochromatic combination, as they are different shades of the same color.

questions.question: 39739. Which of the Lilliputians is the nicest to Gulliver?
questions.explain:
Redresal is the only Lilliputian mentioned in Gulliver's Travels who explicitly shows consistent kindness and concern for Gulliver's well-being. He is the secretary of state for war and is instrumental in helping Gulliver navigate the complexities of Lilliputian court life and politics. He advocates for Gulliver's release from captivity and even proposes a plan to build Gulliver a house suitable for his size. 

Why other options are incorrect: 

Flimnap:
Flimnap is the treasurer and is portrayed as a petty and vindictive individual. He is instrumental in stirring up resentment against Gulliver and plays a key role in the accusations and trials that Gulliver faces.

The Emperor:
While the Emperor initially shows some curiosity and awe towards Gulliver, his actions quickly become motivated by his own power and pride. He uses Gulliver as a spectacle for his court and subjects, and his decisions regarding Gulliver's imprisonment and treatment are largely driven by political considerations rather than genuine concern for Gulliver's welfare.

The Empress:
The Empress is not mentioned specifically in relation to Gulliver's treatment. Her role in the narrative is minimal, and there is no indication of her having any particular interaction with or feelings towards him.

questions.question: 39738. The flying island that Gulliver visited was-
questions.explain: The flying island that Gulliver visited was (খ) Laputa. In Jonathan Swift's Gulliver's Travels, Book 3,  Laputa is described as a large, artificial island that moves by magnetic levitation and is home to an array of scientists, mathematicians, and musicians who are obsessed with their studies. They are so engrossed in their thought that flappers are required to take them from that state.

questions.question: 39737. In a modern interior design, the furniture is arranged asymmetrically but still looks balanced. Which principle is applied here?
questions.explain: Informal balance (Asymmetrical balance) means objects are not identical on both sides of a central axis, but they still create a visual sense of balance.For example, a large sofa on one side can be balanced by two chairs and a lamp on the other side.This principle is often used in modern interior design to create a dynamic and interesting look without being rigid like formal (symmetrical) balance

questions.question: 39736. How many types of harmony can be created with colors? রঙের দ্বারা কয় প্রকার সামঞ্জস্য তৈরি করা যায়?
questions.explain: Three ways: (i) Same color in different shades, (ii) Adjacent colors on the color wheel, (iii) Opposite colors on the color wheel.

questions.question: 39735. Which principle is violated when a room appears overcrowded due to too much furniture in the center? যখন ঘরের মাঝখানে অতিরিক্ত আসবাবপত্র থাকার কারণে ঘর ভরাট দেখায়, তখন কোন নীতি লঙ্ঘিত হয়?
questions.explain: Proportion and harmony are interlinked and complement each other. Harmony means all furniture, pictures, ornaments, and other household items blend well with each other and the house.

questions.question: 39734. Which type of balance involves placing equal visual weight symmetrically on both sides of a centerline? কোন ধরনের সমতা কেন্দ্র রেখার দুই পাশে সমান দৃশ্যমান ওজন সমানভাবে রাখার মাধ্যমে অর্জিত হয়?
questions.option1: Informal Balance
questions.option2: Formal Balance
questions.option3: Visual Balance
questions.option4: Radial Balance
questions.explain: Formal Balance: When equal visual weight is placed symmetrically on both sides of a centerline. For example, placing a large sofa in the center with smaller sofas equidistant on both sides.

questions.question: 39733. Which practice improves both space economy and aesthetic appeal in a small room? ছোট ঘরে কোন প্রয়োগে জায়গার সাশ্রয় ও সৌন্দর্য দুটোই বাড়ে?
questions.option1: Keeping furniture in the center আসবাবপত্র কেন্দ্রে রাখা
questions.option2: Using heavy furniture without proportion সমানুপাত ছাড়াই ভারী আসবাবপত্র ব্যবহার করা
questions.option3: Placing heavy furniture along walls or angles দেয়াল বরাবর বা কোণে ভারী আসবাবপত্র স্থাপন করা
questions.option4: Avoiding space between two pieces of furniture দুটি আসবাবের মধ্যে ফাঁকা স্থান এড়িয়ে চলা
questions.explain: suitability with architecture: Furniture should be consistent with the architecture of the house. Heavy furniture placed parallel to walls or placed appropriately with angles creates a harmonious and varied feeling. Such arrangement also makes small rooms appear larger

questions.question: 39732. Placing a refrigerator near the dining table reflects which aspect of furniture arrangement? ডাইনিং টেবিলের কাছে ফ্রিজ রাখা আসবাবপত্র বিন্যাসের কোন দিককে প্রতিফলিত করে?
questions.option2: Ease of use
questions.explain: Ease of use: While arranging furniture, the practical use of the room must be considered. Each room requires furniture arrangement according to its use. For example, the drawing room or sitting room should be arranged for socializing, hospitality, and enjoyment. The bedroom needs arrangements for comfort, privacy, and personal solitude.

questions.question: 39731. Which of the following is NOT a principle of furniture decoration? নিম্নলিখিত কোনটি আসবাবপত্র বিন্যাসের নীতি নয়?
questions.explain:
The beauty of a room depends largely on the furniture arrangement. Every decorative art form has five basic principles, which also apply to furniture arrangement:
সমানুপাত (Proportion)
সমতা (Balance)
সামঞ্জস্য (Harmony)
ছন্দ (Rhythm)
প্রাধান্য (Emphasis)

questions.question: 39730. Heavy furniture placed parallel to walls or at an angle primarily serves which purpose? দেয়ালের সমান্তরাল বা কোণে ভারী আসবাবপত্র রাখা মূলত কোন উদ্দেশ্য পূরণ করে?
questions.explain: Placing heavy furniture parallel to walls or at an angle creates harmony and variety in the arrangement. It also gives an illusion of more space, making small rooms appear larger.

questions.question: 39729. Which principle creates a sense of equality by distributing visual weight in furniture arrangement? আসবাবপত্র বিন্যাসে কোন নীতি দৃশ্যমান ওজনের সমবন্টন নিশ্চিত করে?
questions.explain: Balance: If furniture is placed on one side of a room, the other side should have something to balance the visual weight. It’s not necessary that the furniture on both sides be exactly the same in size or weight. One side may have large furniture, while the other side can have several smaller pieces to create balance.

questions.question: 39728. Which principle of decorative art ensures that the size of furniture matches the room's dimensions? অলঙ্করণশিল্পের কোন নীতি নিশ্চিত করে যে আসবাবপত্রের আকার ঘরের আকারের সাথে মানানসই?
questions.explain: Proportion means the size and scale of furniture should be in harmony with the space. Large furniture in a small room breaks proportion.

questions.question: 39727. Why should similar types of furniture be grouped together? একই ধরনের আসবাবপত্র একত্রে রাখা কেন প্রয়োজন?
questions.option1: For decoration সাজসজ্জার জন্য
questions.option2: For convenience and unity of function সুবিধার্থে এবং কার্যকারিতার ঐক্যের জন্য
questions.option3: To save money অর্থ সাশ্রয় করার জন্য
questions.option4: To make the room look bigger ঘরটি আরও বড় দেখানোর জন্য
questions.explain: Grouping: Similar types of furniture should be placed together to establish unity of function. This avoids unnecessary movement. For example, keeping a bookshelf near the study table is convenient. Keeping a refrigerator or meat safe near the dining table facilitates serving food.

questions.question: 39726. What is the main purpose of arranging furniture according to the room’s function? কক্ষের উদ্দেশ্য অনুযায়ী আসবাবপত্র সাজানোর প্রধান উদ্দেশ্য কী?
questions.option2: Practical use
questions.option3: Reducing expenses
questions.option4: Space saving
questions.explain: Ease of use: While arranging furniture, the practical use of the room must be considered. Each room requires furniture arrangement according to its use. For example, the drawing room or sitting room should be arranged for socializing, hospitality, and enjoyment. The bedroom needs arrangements for comfort, privacy, and personal solitude.

questions.question: 39725. Why is a rough sketch helpful in furniture arrangement? আসবাবপত্র সাজানোর জন্য খসড়া নকশা কেন সহায়ক?
questions.option1: To increase room size  ঘরের আকার বৃদ্ধি করা
questions.option3: To understand the best placement সর্বোত্তম স্থান নির্ধারণ করা
questions.option4: To avoid buying furniture আসবাবপত্র কেনা এড়িয়ে চলা
questions.explain: Neat arrangement: First and foremost, ensure that no room has excessive furniture. Too much furniture spoils the beauty instead of enhancing it. Making a rough sketch of the furniture layout before arranging helps to understand where each piece will look best. Changing the furniture arrangement occasionally can bring freshness. Keeping the same furniture in the same place for a long time causes boredom.

questions.question: 39724. A chemical-industry parent wants to launch baby-care products. Best branding move? (কেমিক্যাল-ইন্ডাস্ট্রি প্যারেন্ট বেবি-কেয়ার চালু করতে চায়—সেরা ব্র্যান্ডিং পছন্দ?)
questions.explain:
Parent associations (“industrial chemicals”)conflict with baby-care meanings (safety/gentleness); a new brand avoids negative transfer and enables suitable positioning, packaging, and channels.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39723. Which situation signals a communication gap? (কোন পরিস্থিতি কমিউনিকেশন গ্যাপ নির্দেশ করে?)
questions.option1: Don’t know expectations / গ্রাহক প্রত্যাশা অজানা
questions.option2: Ads promise more than operations deliver / বিজ্ঞাপনে অপারেশনের চেয়ে বেশি প্রতিশ্রুতি
questions.explain:
The communication gap arises when external messaging misaligns with actual delivery capacity, creating disappointment; fix by aligning promise with process and capacity.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39722. Which is a non-physical rate fence in yield management? (ইয়িল্ড ম্যানেজমেন্টে কোনটি নন-ফিজিক্যাল রেট ফেন্স?)
questions.explain:
Non-physical fences segment buyers by booking conditions (such as advance purchase, refundability, and minimum stay) rather than tangible features; physical fences are typically based on seat class, room size, and amenities.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8

questions.question:
39721. A mid-tier smartphone brand “Mobi” wants to win the lowest-price segment in the same category without eroding Mobi’s equity. Which path is best?
​ (মাঝারি দামের স্মার্টফোন ব্র্যান্ড “Mobi” একই ক্যাটাগরিতে সর্বনিম্ন দামের সেগমেন্ট জিততে চায়, কিন্তু Mobi-র ইক্যুইটি ক্ষয় করতে চায় না। সেরা পথ কোনটি?)
questions.option1: Line extension under Mobi / “Mobi”-র অধীনে লাইন এক্সটেনশন
questions.option2: Brand extension under Mobi / “Mobi” নামে ব্র্যান্ড এক্সটেনশন
questions.option3: Multibrand fighter with clear fences / স্পষ্ট ফেন্সসহ মাল্টিব্র্যান্ড ফাইটার
questions.option4: New brand in a new category / নতুন ক্যাটাগরিতে নতুন ব্র্যান্ড
questions.explain:
Addressing an entry-price tier in the same category under the flagship risks dilution and trading-down; a multibrand fighter can carry stripped features, different packs/channels, and explicit price–feature fences so Mobi’s mid-tier promise remains intact while the firm competes at the bottom.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39720. Best pretest to gauge brand-extension fit before launch is- (লঞ্চের আগে ব্র্যান্ড এক্সটেনশনের ফিট মাপার সেরা প্রি-টেস্ট-)
questions.option3: Consumer concept testing on benefit/ভোক্তা কনসেপ্ট টেস্ট (উপকার)
questions.option4: Sales forecast from finance / ফাইন্যান্স বিভাগের বিক্রয় পূর্বাভাস
questions.explain:
Perceived fit (benefits, usage occasions, and attribute transfer) predicts extension success; concept tests, sometimes followed by conjoint/sim-market, estimate acceptance and cannibalization risk better than internal costing.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39719. To reduce risk of genericide for a strong mark, firms should- (শক্তিশালী ট্রেডমার্ককে জেনেরিসাইড থেকে বাঁচাতে করণীয়-)
questions.option1: Use as a noun / বিশেষ্য হিসেবে ব্যবহার
questions.option2: Use as adjective + enforce proper usage + educate media / বিশেষণ হিসেবে ব্যবহার + সঠিক ব্যবহার নিশ্চিত + মিডিয়াকে শিক্ষিত করা
questions.option3: Allow free use / অবাধ ব্যবহার অনুমতি
questions.explain:
Prevent marks from becoming generic by using them as adjectives (“Brand® tissues”), policing misuse, and educating partners/media; legal enforcement sustains protectability.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39718.  In a service blueprint, the line of visibility separates- (সার্ভিস ব্লুপ্রিন্টে লাইন অফ ভিজিবিলিটি আলাদা করে-)
questions.option1: Front vs supplier / ফ্রন্ট বনাম সরবরাহকারী
questions.option2: On-stage vs backstage actions / অন-স্টেজ বনাম ব্যাকস্টেজ কার্যাবলি
questions.option3: Staff vs customers / কর্মী বনাম গ্রাহক
questions.option4: Design vs promotion / নকশা বনাম প্রচারণা
questions.explain:
The visibility line distinguishes what customers see from backstage processes that enable delivery; locating failures against this line guides fixes (training vs systems).
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8

questions.question: 39717. Ethically defensible overbooking in services requires- (নৈতিকভাবে গ্রহণযোগ্য ওভারবুকিং করতে প্রয়োজন-)
questions.option2: Predictable no-shows + transparent rules + fair compensation / পূর্বানুমেয় নো-শো + স্বচ্ছ নিয়ম + ন্যায্য ক্ষতিপূরণ
questions.option4: First-come only / কেবল আগে এলে আগে পাবেন
questions.explain:
Because capacity is perishable, modest overbooking can increase utilization if no-show rates are factored in and customers are protected through clear disclosures, priority booking, and compensation/alternatives; otherwise, reputational damage outweighs the gains.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8

questions.question:
39716. Which proposed brand name is most likely to satisfy protectability and transferability for potential future category moves?
​ (ভবিষ্যতে নতুন ক্যাটাগরিতে যাওয়ার সম্ভাবনা থাকলে প্রোটেক্টেবিলিটি ও ট্রান্সফারেবিলিটি—উভয়দিক থেকেই কোন নামটি বেশি উপযোগী?)
questions.option3: ZYRA” (coined), for appliances today, other home goods later / “ZYRA” (নতুন গঠিত), এখন অ্যাপ্লায়েন্স, পরে অন্যান্য হোম গুডস
questions.option4: “BlueLeaf” for organic tea / অর্গানিক চা-র জন্য “BlueLeaf”
questions.explain:
Coined/arbitrary names like “ZYRA” are typically more distinctive (protectable) and transferable across categories/markets than generic/descriptive names (e.g., “TeaLeaf” is generic within tea; “FreshCold” is descriptive for ACs). A suggestive name like “BlueLeaf” can work for tea, but is less transferable beyond beverages.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 9

questions.question: 39715. Self-service technology primarily helps mitigate which IHIP issue? (সেল্‌ফ-সার্ভিস টেকনোলজি IHIP-এর কোন সমস্যাটি প্রধানত কমায়?)
questions.explain:
SSTs standardize execution and reduce human variability (ensuring the same flow each time), often improving responsiveness; they don’t eliminate perishability and may partially reduce inseparability through asynchronous tasks.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8

questions.question: 39714. Which is an ambient servicescape element? (কোনটি অ্যাম্বিয়েন্ট সার্ভিসস্কেপ উপাদান?)
questions.explain:
Servicescape spans ambient conditions (temperature, scent, sound), spatial/design (layout, furnishings), and social factors (staff density). Ambient cues strongly shape affect and perceived quality.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8

questions.question: 39713. In services, which tactic most accelerates adoption of self-service kiosks? (সার্ভিসে সেল্‌ফ-সার্ভিস কিয়স্ক দ্রুত গ্রহণে কোন কৌশল বেশি কার্যকর?)
questions.option2: On-site coaching + clear UI cues + small incentives / অন-সাইট কোচিং + স্পষ্ট UI সংকেত + ছোট প্রণোদনা
questions.option4: Staff removal day-1 / প্রথম দিনেই স্টাফ অপসারণ
questions.explain:
Guided trials, visible wayfinding/UI, and token incentives reduce anxiety and signal benefits (speed/control) while preserving help for novices; abrupt staff removal backfires.
​
​​​References: Kotler et al. (2022), Principles of Marketing, Ch. 8
